newsitem.title: INDIA: Rebels ambush Indian security patrol, kill 19.
newsitem.headline: Rebels ambush Indian security patrol, kill 19.

text.p: Separatist tribal guerrillas ambushed a security patrol in northeastern India on Wednesday and shot dead 18 paramilitary soldiers and a policeman, state police said.

"A group of National Liberation Front of Tripura (NLFT) militants this morning ambushed a Central Reserve Police Force patrol party and killed 17 CRPF personnel and a state policeman," police superintendent Bibhuti Chaudhury told Reuters in the capital of Tripura state, Agartala.

Three paramilitary soldiers were critically wounded in the attack, which occurred in southern Tripura's Natunbazar area at 8:30 a.m. (0300 GMT). Chaudhury later said a CRPF soldier, wounded in the attack, had died.
The NLFT is an outlawed guerrilla group that has been fighting for a separate homeland since 1989.
The Communist Party of India-Marxist, which rules Tripura, called for a general strike in southern parts of the state on Thursday to protest against the killings.

The state government asked the army and paramilitary troops to search for the insurgents, Chaudhury said. The rebels had stolen the dead soldiers' weapons and vanished into the forests surrounding the mountainous region, he said.
State Home (Interior) Minister Samar Chaudhury told reporters: "The government will take stern action against all the insurgent outfits."
In February, a different group of tribal guerrillas, the All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF), killed at least 50 people in west Tripura, setting houses ablaze and leaving thousands homeless.

The federal government then granted sweeping shoot-on-sight powers to army troops deployed in the thickly wooded northeastern state and authorised army and paramilitary reinforcements to arrest and indefinitely detain suspects.
Last July, the ATTF issued a statement warning Bengali settlers to leave the state, which shares an 840-km (520-mile) border with Bangladesh to the west.
The state's indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who dominate local politics and the economy.
Tribal militants have been pursuing a campaign seeking a separate state for 17 years. More than 2,000 people were killed in the region's worst ethnic riots in June 1980.
